LESSON: READING 11.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.2: Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why is it important to relate what you read to real life experiences?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. create mental images from the events, characters or places in a text
2. answer direct and inferential questions from varied texts correctly

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. create mental images from the events, characters or places in a text
   In simple words: practise until you can create mental images from the events, characters or places in a text. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. answer direct and inferential questions from varied texts correctly
   In simple words: practise until you can answer direct and inferential questions from varied texts correctly. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading.
4. Show that you can: create mental images from the events, characters or places in a text

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 11.2.1 Intensive Reading important for a Grade 5 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Search and read texts from the internet with peers,
2. Dramatise or role play events or characters in stories they have read online,
3. Critical Thinking and Problem Solving is cultivated as the learner engages in research online.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to relate what you read to real life experiences?
2. What digital resources can you use in your reading?
3. Why are digital materials more interesting to read than print ones?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. create mental images from the events, characters or places in a text
2. answer direct and inferential questions from varied texts correctly

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
